# Category verdict, method v2.1 (2026-11-08)

Supersedes `work/blind/FINAL_V2.md`. Same rules (/RUNBOOK.md, rules 1-6); changes from v2.0 are listed in the RUNBOOK version log.
What changed in the data: Amazon now read with a US delivery address (ZIP 10001) — 16 categories by script, 4 collected by hand by the owner's assistant; Meta counted for all 20 categories with a 30-day window; brand ads counted on the brand's own Facebook Page; Google Trends pull 1 of 3.

## Verdict (judgment on top of the table — written, not computed)

| Status | Category | Why, in one line |
|---|---|---|
| **#1** | Color-changing foundation | Every layer positive: 211,800 units/mo to brands under 24 months old, search interest ×4.7 a year, the most ads (12,000) and two brands (Smooche, Prime Prometics) with hundreds of ads alive 180+ days on their own Pages. |
| **#2** | Body oil for crepey skin | A shelf of old brands (Palmer's, Neutrogena), but one newcomer, GODA, reached 20,000/mo on Amazon and runs through creator pages on Meta: proof that a new brand can break in. |
| **#3** | Waterless scent diffuser | Highest price ($64 median), search ×2.0, AirScent (23 months) at 11,100/mo; on Meta Scentify keeps ads alive 2+ years. Half of Amazon units go to unbranded sellers: a store-plus-Meta play, not an Amazon one. |
| **#4** | Beef tallow balm | Most newcomer wins (9 brands ≥1K/mo, 45,550 units), many small shops with evergreen Meta ads, but search growth has stopped (×1.05). |
| **#5** | Persimmon soap | Fastest-growing search (×4.6) and active Meta testing, but the pie is small, the old leader Mirai holds 25,300 of 69,550 units, and new brands take only 7,350. |
| challenger (compliance) | Eyelash growth serum | Big shelf (213,450) and 8 new-brand winners, but old brands hold 2/3, growth claims make it a regulated product, and brand ages are estimated, not dated. |
| challenger (compliance) | Hair-growth serum | Same picture (240,900 shelf, 8 new winners, 31,650 to new brands) plus overlap with rosemary oil, whose demand is falling. |
| reserve | Filtered shower head | Old brands hold 2/3 of the shelf; strongest evergreen Meta advertiser of all (sproos: 94 of 130 ads alive 180+ days). |
| weak | Pre-wash hair oil, men's hair removal cream, neck cream, pet fountain, chin wrap, pore patches, compression socks, teeth whitening powder, magnesium spray, exfoliating towel | Each fails at least one of: new brands under ~10,000 units/mo, shelf held by 1-2 old brands, Amazon dominated by unbranded sellers, or no measurable Meta market. Details per page. |
| dropped (rule 5a) | Rosemary hair oil, turmeric soap | Search interest falling (×0.76, ×0.67 a year). |

Order of #1-#5 is unchanged from v2.0 on purpose: the new data did not contradict it, and the owner asked for a stable method. The two serums would rank near #2-#3 on Amazon openness alone; they are held back by the regulatory cost and by undated brand ages.

## Known limits (said on every page)
- Kill rule 5b is weak in practice: the Meta sample is drawn by age window, so any category with at least one 90d+ ad shows a shop with a 90d+ ad. Only pore patches came close to failing it.
- Amazon brand detection reads the title; 22 of 72 top listings checked by hand carry a registered brand not in the title (LATORICE, NXPPYY...). They are counted as unbranded sellers, which is how they behave (price-led), but the label is "registered brand without a known name".
- Trend = 1 pull of 3; pulls 2-3 on 2026-11-09 and 11-10 may move borderline labels (neck cream 1.19, chin wrap 0.84, pore patches 0.81).
- Not measured: traffic, review growth over time, margins, stopped ads before 2026-11-08.
